game: Kent State Golden Flashes@Ohio State Buckeyes

guide_enrichment.narrative:
What stands out to us is how closely the market’s large number matches the underlying mismatch. Kent State grades poorly in both rushing efficiency and scoring-opportunity creation, while Ohio State rates among the strongest defenses in preventing both. Ohio State also held Ball State to 165 total yards in its opener, though we are not treating one result as proof that the defense has fully reloaded.

The more difficult issue for Kent State is Ohio State’s offensive ceiling. Julian Sayin returns after completing 77.0 percent of his passes last season, and the offensive line entered 2026 with a reported 85.8 percent continuity rate. The Buckeyes then produced 671 yards in the opener. Ohio State did lose eight defensive starters and returns only three, which adds some uncertainty at an extreme margin, but our numbers do not show enough meaningful disagreement with the market to justify taking Kent State at the available price.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, the matchup to watch is Kent State’s rushing offense against Ohio State’s rebuilt front. Our efficiency numbers show a substantial advantage for the defense, and Ohio State allowed only 45 rushing yards against Ball State. The personnel turnover gives Kent State at least a question to test, but if the Flashes cannot generate efficient early-down runs, their path to sustaining drives becomes especially narrow.

recent_game.fact: Ohio State opened the 2026 season with a 56-3 home win over Ball State on Sept. 5.
Against Ball State, Ohio State produced 671 total yards, including 434 passing and 237 rushing, and converted 45.5 percent of its third downs.
Ohio State held Ball State to 165 total yards, including 45 rushing and 120 passing, and allowed conversions on 21.4 percent of third downs.
Fourteen Ohio State players caught a pass against Ball State, the program's first game with at least 14 receivers recording a catch since Sept. 22, 2018, against Tulane.
Jeremiah Smith caught eight passes for 151 yards and two touchdowns against Ball State, with all of that production coming in the first half.
Bo Jackson averaged 9.2 yards per carry in the opener and scored on a career-long 65-yard run.
Freshman Legend Bey had 100 all-purpose yards against Ball State and scored on his first career reception.
Ohio State played 21 true freshmen in the season opener against Ball State.

quarterback.fact: Julian Sayin returns as Ohio State's starting quarterback after starting 15 of his 19 career games.

In 2025, Sayin completed 77.0 percent of his passes for 3,610 yards, 32 touchdowns and eight interceptions; his completion percentage led the nation and set Ohio State and Big Ten single-season records.
Sayin has seven career 300-yard passing games.
Reserve quarterback Justyn Martin has appeared in six career games and has no starts.

offensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returns eight offensive starters: quarterback Julian Sayin, running back Bo Jackson, wide receivers Jeremiah Smith and Brandon Inniss, tackle Phillip Daniels, center Carson Hinzman, and guards Luke Montgomery and Austin Siereveld.
Ohio State lost three offensive starters from 2025: guard Tegra Tshabola and tight ends Max Klare and Will Kacmarek.
Ohio State reports an 85.8 percent offensive-line continuity rate, the highest among Power Four teams, based on returning snaps from players who logged at least 100 snaps in 2025.
After the season opener, Ohio State's starting offensive line had combined for 146 games played and 93 starts.
Center Carson Hinzman has 36 starts in 39 career games, Austin Siereveld has 21 starts in 25 games, Phillip Daniels has 17 starts in 26 games and Luke Montgomery has 17 starts in 37 games.
Bo Jackson returns after leading Ohio State with 1,090 rushing yards on 179 carries in 2025.
Jeremiah Smith entered the second game of 2026 with 171 career receptions, 2,709 receiving yards and 29 receiving touchdowns.
Wide receiver Devin McCuin transferred from UTSA after making 65 catches for 726 yards and eight touchdowns in 2025; he has 28 career starts.
Wide receiver Kyle Parker transferred from LSU with 34 career receptions for 385 yards and five touchdowns in 21 games, including seven starts.
Ohio State's experienced tight ends include Hunter Welcing, who has 11 career starts, Mason Williams, who has 26 career starts, and Bennett Christian, who has two career starts.

defensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returns three defensive starters: cornerback Jermaine Mathews Jr., defensive end Kenyatta Jackson Jr. and safety Jaylen McClain.

Ohio State lost eight defensive starters from 2025: defensive tackles Tywone Malone Jr. and Kayden McDonald, defensive end Caden Curry, linebackers Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles, safeties Caleb Downs and Lorenzo Styles, and cornerback Devin Igbinosun.
Defensive tackle James Smith transferred from Alabama after recording 28 tackles, 6.5 tackles for loss and 2.5 sacks in 2025.
Defensive end Qua Russaw transferred from Alabama with 50 career tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss, two sacks and two interceptions.
Linebacker Christian Alliegro transferred from Wisconsin with 127 career tackles and eight sacks across 36 games and 12 starts.
Defensive tackle John Walker transferred from UCF with 64 career tackles, eight tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks in 26 games.
Safety Earl Little Jr. transferred from Florida State after leading the Seminoles with 76 tackles in 2025; he has 97 tackles and four interceptions in 37 career games.
Kenyatta Jackson Jr. entered 2026 with 56 career tackles and 9.5 sacks, including 11 tackles for loss and 6.5 sacks in 2025.
Safety Jaylen McClain made 53 tackles and played 816 defensive snaps in 2025.

coaching_changes.fact: Ohio State's 2026 staff lists Matt Patricia as defensive coordinator and Arthur Smith as offensive coordinator.
Tyler Bowen is Ohio State's run game coordinator and offensive line coach, while Billy Fessler is the pass game coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
Robby Discher is Ohio State's special teams coordinator.

offensive_context.fact: Ohio State scored 56 points and gained 671 total yards in its 2026 opener, with 434 passing yards and 237 rushing yards.
Ohio State converted every red-zone opportunity against Ball State.
Since Ryan Day became head coach in 2019, Ohio State has averaged 39.6 points per game and has scored at least 50 points in 23 games.
Ohio State is one of two FBS programs, along with Miami, to have a 3,500-yard passer, a 1,000-yard receiver and a 1,000-yard rusher in each of the previous two seasons.

defensive_context.fact: Ohio State allowed three points and 165 total yards in its 2026 opener, including 45 rushing yards and 120 passing yards.
Ball State converted 21.4 percent of its third downs and did not score on a red-zone possession against Ohio State.
Ohio State allowed 9.3 points and 219.1 total yards per game in 2025, ranking first nationally in scoring defense and total defense.
Ohio State allowed 129.7 passing yards per game in 2025 and 8.73 yards per completion.
Since the start of the 2024 season, Ohio State has allowed 37 touchdowns in 31 games and has held nine opponents without a touchdown.

special_teams.fact: Punter Joe McGuire is Ohio State's only returning specialist starter.
Ohio State lost starting kicker Jayden Fielding and long snapper John Ferlmann from the 2025 team.

other_relevant.fact: Ohio State is scheduled to host Kent State at noon on FOX on Sept. 19, 2026.
Ohio State entered its second game of 2026 with a 1-0 record and was ranked No. 1 in the Associated Press poll.
